messages:
aj: quick check — i'm about to land a terraform change that consolidates per-model runtime knobs into a single ConfigMap per model (was scattered across overlays). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/6789

aj: main question: do we need a special rollout handshake with the serving pods or will annotating the deployment with a checksum and triggering a rolling restart be enough?

maya: +1 on checksum annotation approach. avoids kube magic. we do need to ensure pods pick up the mounted configmap at start or via a sidecar refresh.

kevin: what does the tf resource look like? paste snippet?

aj: here — small excerpt from the k8s manifest we plan to render via terraform:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-{{ model_name }}-runtime
  namespace: inference-{{ env }}
  annotations:
    redwood.com/config-checksum: "${sha256(file(\"model-${model_name}-config.yaml\"))}"
data:
  runtime.json: |
    { "max_seq": 2048, "quant_mode": "q4_0", "feature_flags": { "xy_cache": true }}
```

samir: if you're using terraform to render, make sure the sha256 value is computed in the CI step, not at apply time. terraform will otherwise treat it as a dynamic value and you'll get churn.

maya: add to that — we should keep sensitive knobs in a Secret and mount both. configmap for non-sensitive toggles. avoids accidental leak in logs.

aj: yep — plan is configmap + secret fallback. fallback logic lives in startup: if secret exists, merge secrets over configmap.

kevin: for rolling semantics, annotate the deployment template with the same checksum so k8s triggers a rollout when config changes:```yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        redwood.com/config-checksum: "${redwood.com/config-checksum}"
```

samir: also consider a canary label for 5% of traffic for the first 10 minutes, so we can watch latency/regressions. we have a canned rollout job: infra/playbooks/config-rollout-canary.md

aj: good call. i can wire a kustomize overlay that sets replicas: 2 and label: canary=true for the canary. snippet in the PR.

maya: minor nits: update the k8s liveness/readiness to tolerate config-merge delay. we had an incident where readiness failed until the sidecar finished merging. basically bump initialDelaySeconds by 10.

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for branch aj/configmap-consolidation — no surprise changes to prod resources. plan id: tp-20231122-54

infra-bot: reminder: when you flip the configmap key names make sure the per-model operator has the mapping in the next operator release, otherwise older reloader wont find them.

aj: noted — will add an operator compat shim and a migration job to copy legacy keys to the new shape.

kevin: PR reviewers: @maya, @samir — pinged in the PR. can we aim to merge by EOD today if infra checks are green?

maya: i can review after standup. will focus on teardown/migration job to avoid double-writes.

samir: i'll run the canary rollout once merged and watch the per-route latency dashboard. if anything spikes we'll revert and fallback to the old configmap mount.

aj: thanks — assigning myself to the migration job and i'll post results here. TL;DR: configmap consolidation + checksum annotation + secret fallback + canary rollout.

kevin: ack :thumbsup:

aj: follow-up: added a tiny helper bash in the PR to compute checksum in CI:```bash
# CI compute checksum for model config
sha256sum model-${MODEL_NAME}-config.yaml | awk '{print $1}' > checksum.txt
```

maya: lgtm on the CI step. just make sure we store checksum as a CI artifact so infra plan can pick it up.

aj: will do. posting merge + canary results here once complete.

samir: thanks — appreciate the heads up.
